Title: Unison
Description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) is soliciting innovative proposals for Unison, a program to develop and evaluate collaborative-autonomy approaches that jointly adapt team decision-making and communications during mission execution. Unison will investigate approaches that enable autonomous teams to modify tactics, behaviors, coordination relationships, and information exchange as mission complexity and operational variability increase and communications become constrained and/or degraded (see Section 7, Glossary, for program-specific definitions of terms in italics). The core hypothesis of Unison is that a unified execution-time reasoning approach to action planning and communications planning can improve the effectiveness, scalability, and resilience of collaborative autonomy in dynamic, uncertain, and resource-constrained environments. Unison seeks to preserve mission performance while reducing communication dependence and bounding the reasoning burden imposed on individual agents. Unison frames collaborative autonomy as a multi-agent decision problem in which agents use local observations, mission context, relevance, and mission objectives to select a policy that jointly defines physical actions and communications actions. At each decision point, the team must determine what actions to take, which coordination relationships must be maintained, and what information must be exchanged to preserve the coordination required for mission success. Unison will investigate approaches across teams of tens to hundreds of agents operating in representative collaborative, multi-domain mission scenarios.

Title: Post Quantum Cryptography (PQC) Readiness and Validation Status
Office: FC ACQUISITION SOLUTIONS DEV/IDV ACQ MANAGEMENT
Description: https://feedback.gsa.gov/jfe/form/SV_3t6dNlgkS4Vg6iy Federal agencies are preparing for the transition from cryptographic algorithms that may be vulnerable to future quantum computing attacks to quantum-resistant cryptographic algorithms standardized by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). Public key cryptographic algorithms (i.e. asymmetric cryptography) currently used across Federal information systems, products and services — including Rivest-Shamir-Adleman (RSA), elliptic curve Diffie-Hellman(ECDH), elliptic curve digital signature algorithms (ECDSA), and related mechanisms — will be vulnerable to a future cryptanalytically relevant quantum computer (CRQC). As a result, Federal agencies are expected to identify, prioritize, and migrate quantum-vulnerable cryptographic systems to approved post-quantum cryptographic algorithms. Federal agencies are also required to use validated cryptographic algorithms and modules when cryptography is required to protect Federal information or Federal systems. The NIST Cryptographic Module Validation Program establishes requirements under FIPS 140-2 and FIPS 140-3. FIPS 140-2 and FIPS 140-3 requirements are applicable to U.S. Federal agencies when cryptographic-based security systems are used to provide information security for Federal operations and assets. If cryptography is required for the protection of information or data, then FIPS-validated cryptography is applicable. Non-validated cryptography shall be treated as providing no validated protection for Federal information where validated cryptography is required. Relevant policy, standards, and guidance include, but may not be limited to: NIST Cryptographic Module Validation Program; FIPS 140-2 and FIPS 140-3, Security Requirements for Cryptographic Modules; FIPS 203, Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism Standard; FIPS 204, Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Standard; FIPS 205, Stateless Hash-Based Digital Signature Standard; NIST SP 800-208, Recommendation for Stateful Hash-Based Signature Schemes; NIST SP 800-52, Guidelines for the Selection, Configuration, and Use of Transport Layer Security Implementations; OMB Memorandum M-22-09, Moving the U.S. Government Toward Zero Trust Cybersecurity Principles; Executive Order 14306, Sustaining Select Efforts to Strengthen the Nation’s Cybersecurity; Executive Order 14412, Securing the Nation Against Advanced Cryptographic Attacks; OMB Memorandum M-26-15, Execution of the Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography; and CISA guidance regarding product categories and technologies that use post-quantum cryptography standards. This RFI is intended to collect industry information regarding the availability, validation status, product and service readiness, procurement accessibility, implementation maturity, operational impacts, interoperability, and migration support associated with commercial products and services that support, or plan to support, NIST-approved post-quantum cryptography standards. This Request for Information is issued for market research purposes only. There are no anticipated tasks under this RFI. This RFI is intended to collect information from industry regarding vendor capabilities, products and services availability, cryptographic validation status, contract accessibility, and readiness to support the Federal Government’s migration to post-quantum cryptography (PQC). This RFI does not constitute a solicitation, Request for Proposal, Request for Quotation, Invitation for Bid, or promise to issue a future solicitation. Title: Unison
Description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) is soliciting innovative proposals for Unison, a program to develop and evaluate collaborative-autonomy approaches that jointly adapt team decision-making and communications during mission execution. Unison will investigate approaches that enable autonomous teams to modify tactics, behaviors, coordination relationships, and information exchange as mission complexity and operational variability increase and communications become constrained and/or degraded (see Section 7, Glossary, for program-specific definitions of terms in italics). The core hypothesis of Unison is that a unified execution-time reasoning approach to action planning and communications planning can improve the effectiveness, scalability, and resilience of collaborative autonomy in dynamic, uncertain, and resource-constrained environments. Unison seeks to preserve mission performance while reducing communication dependence and bounding the reasoning burden imposed on individual agents. Unison frames collaborative autonomy as a multi-agent decision problem in which agents use local observations, mission context, relevance, and mission objectives to select a policy that jointly defines physical actions and communications actions. At each decision point, the team must determine what actions to take, which coordination relationships must be maintained, and what information must be exchanged to preserve the coordination required for mission success. Unison will investigate approaches across teams of tens to hundreds of agents operating in representative collaborative, multi-domain mission scenarios.

Title: DLA-RFI-CT-2027-WBOS-MKTRES
Description: DEFENSE LOGISTICS AGENCY (DLA) TROOP SUPPORT CLOTHING AND TEXTILES DIRECTORATE — PHILADELPHIA, PA REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) & SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Whole-of-Government Web-Based Ordering System (WBOS) & Commercial eMarketplace Platform FEDERAL MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE (FAR 15.201(e) & FAR Part 10): This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for market research, planning, and information-gathering purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO), or an obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services. The Government is seeking broad industry input on commercial capabilities, architectural options, and market readiness. Responses are strictly voluntary; the Government will not reimburse any costs associated with preparing or submitting responses to this notice. 1. Executive Summary & Purpose of Inquiry The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Troop Support Clothing and Textiles (C&T) Directorate is conducting market research to explore commercial software solutions, digital eMarketplace architectures, and industry best practices for deploying a next-generation Web-Based Ordering System (WBOS). DLA’s Troop Support C&T organization serves as the Federal Government’s primary enterprise manager for military clothing and textiles, working extensively with domestic industry. DLA is currently assessing the expansion of this shared-services procurement model to serve civilian Whole-of-Government (WOG) partner agencies, including the Department of the Interior (DOI), Department of Justice (DOJ), Department of Transportation (DOT), Department of State (DOS), and Department of Homeland Security (DHS). The primary objective of this RFI is to engage commercial e-commerce developers, SaaS providers, systems integrators, and domestic textile industry stakeholders. DLA seeks to understand what commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) and Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) capabilities exist today, how commercial technology can resolve complex federal supply chain and fiscal integration challenges, and what industry recommendations DLA should incorporate into its upcoming acquisition strategy. DLA is committed to adopting commercial best practices and avoiding custom development wherever commercial platforms can satisfy or be adapted to meet mission requirements. 2. Administrative Overview & Acquisition Milestones Market Research Parameter: Information & Acquisition Guidance Document Identifier: DLA-RFI-CT-2027-WBOS-MKTRES Anticipated Acquisition Approach: Commercial Solutions Opening (10 U.S.C. § 3458) / Commercial Acquisition (FAR Part 12 / Agile Authorities) Primary NAICS Code: 541512 - Computer Systems Design Services (Small Business Size Standard: $34.0M) Secondary NAICS Codes: 518210 - Data Processing, Hosting, and Related Services ($40.0M), 541519 - Other Computer Related Services ($34.0M) Product Service Code (PSC): DA01 - IT and Telecom - Business Application/Application Development Software RFI Issuance Date: Friday, October 30, 2026 Industry Questions & Clarifications Due: Friday, November 06, 2026, at 16:00 EST Government Formal Q&A Responses Posted: Friday, November 20, 2026 RFI Capability Response Deadline: Friday, November 27, 2026, at 16:00 EST Anticipated Pre-Solicitation Industry Day: December 2, 2026 (Virtual) Primary Contract Specialist: Courtney Hunter, Contract Specialist, DLA Troop Support C&T (Courtney.Hunter@dla.mil) Primary Contracting Officer: Ryan Zarkowski, Individual Protection and Commercial Solutions Division Chief, DLA Troop Support (Ryan.Zarkowski@dla.mil) Submission Channel: Electronic submission via email to Government POCs (Subject: 'WBOS RFI Response - [Company Name]') 3. Mission Needs & Strategic Challenges The contemplated capability would enable Government-approved vendors to list and maintain Government-approved catalogs; enable authorized agency personnel to purchase authorized items; apply agency-specific eligibility, entitlement/allowance, item-authorization, approval, and management-control rules; support authorized payment methods; and provide auditable transaction, fulfillment, and program-management information. To modernize uniform procurement across DoD and civilian partner agencies, any future solution must address several interrelated operational and regulatory challenges. Rather than dictating prescriptive technical designs, DLA outlines the desired functional outcomes below to invite innovative, industry-driven solutions: Operational Domain: The Operational Challenge / Desired Outcome Commercial Marketplace & User Experience: Deliver a modern, consumer-grade multi-tenant e-commerce experience with sub-second catalog search, faceted filtering, mobile responsiveness, and intuitive uniform selection, while supporting distinct tenant agency branding (DoD, DOI, DOJ, DOT, DOS, DHS) and role-based permissions. Domestic Provenance & Supply Chain Integrity: Because DLA operates as a central procurement hub utilizing the Defense Working Capital Fund (DWCF), end-items transacted through DLA are subject to 100% domestic sourcing requirements under the Berry Amendment (10 U.S.C. § 4862). DLA requires automated mechanisms to verify domestic origin down to the raw material/mill level, screen supply chains for forced labor or prohibited foreign entities, and prevent unverified items from being purchased. Statutory Competition & Micro-Purchases: In a multi-vendor marketplace environment, transactions must respect federal competition mandates (such as CICA and simplified acquisition thresholds). The Government seeks automated, user-friendly marketplace workflows that promote fair competition, facilitate dynamic quoting between micro-purchase thresholds ($15k) and simplified acquisition threshold ($350k), and prevent improper order splitting without creating administrative bottlenecks. Uniform Customization & Value-Added Logistics: Civilian law enforcement and military personnel require customized uniforms (e.g., branch tapes, badges, department patches, embroidery, reflective safety trims, and tailored sizing). The system must support interactive customization, dimensionally accurate digital proofing, supervisor approvals, and tracking of value-added tailoring services while ensuring all component materials remain compliant. Interagency Accounting & Fiscal Guardrails: The system must handle interagency funding across diverse partner departments without risking Antideficiency Act (ADA) violations. This includes integrating with federal financial frameworks (such as Treasury G-Invoicing Form 7600A/B), managing annual individual officer uniform allowances (5 U.S.C. § 5901), supporting multi-payment split tender (allowance + GPC + personal card overages), and reconciling DLA cost-recovery surcharges without contractor fee retention. Cybersecurity & Enterprise Interoperability: The platform will process sensitive federal uniform requisitions, military supply chain data, and law enforcement personnel information. It must meet high federal cybersecurity baselines (such as FedRAMP and DoD Cloud Computing Security Requirements), support CAC/PIV single sign-on, and interface with federal backbones such as DLA Enterprise Business System (EBS/SAP), PIEE/WAWF, and SAM.gov. Training & Performance Tracking: Provide general user training, program manager training, etc. Implement all necessary work and time management control processes to ensure timely accurate accomplishment of work requirements as well as to permit tracking work in progress. 4. Areas of Inquiry & Market Research Questionnaire Industry respondents are invited to address the following questions. Offerors may respond to all or selected inquiry areas based on their core competencies and commercial experience. 4.1 Pillar 1: Market Position & Differentiation Question 1.1 (Core Competencies): Outline your primary services and expertise, such as previous projects in a similar scope, or any COTS options you currently offer. Question 1.2 (Value Proposition): What are your differentiators or unique selling propositions? Are there any facets that make your company standout such as a superior development system, API integration experience with the platforms mentioned? 4.2 Pillar 2: Commercial Marketplace Architecture & User Experience Question 2.1 (Platform Scalability & Multi-Tenancy): How does, or could, your commercial platform support multi-tenant architectures where different cabinet agencies (e.g., FBI, Border Patrol, National Park Service, Diplomatic Security) require custom-branded storefronts, restricted role-based product catalogs, and agency-specific approval hierarchies within a unified infrastructure? Question 2.2 (Interactive Customization & Proofing): How do commercial e-commerce platforms handle complex item personalization (e.g., applying patches, rank insignia, name tapes, custom embroidery, and sizing alterations)? What self-service visual design canvas, dimensional 3D proofing, or digital mock-up capabilities exist in your solution to ensure buyer approval prior to order release? Question 2.3 (Two-Layer Decoupling): In federal enterprise marketplaces, how can the core software platform (the technology gateway and catalog hosting) be effectively decoupled from third-party physical goods fulfillment, ensuring transparent supplier onboarding and open commercial competition without software scope overlap? Question 2.4 (Reporting): Describe the Government’s ability to access, export, retain, and transition data during and after contract performance. Question 2.5 (Proprietary Information): Identify any proprietary data formats, licensing restrictions, third-party dependencies, or other factors that could affect transition to another provider. 4.3 Pillar 3: Cost & Timeline Question 3.1 (Cost): What is the estimated cost associated with this WBOS/eMarketplace? What is the breakdown of the yearly upkeep costs? Question 3.2 (Timeline): What is the timeline to provide a fully functional WBOS/ eMarketplace? What hurdles do you foresee that might extend the timeline? How close is your current system to being fully functional based on the Government’s needs? 4.4 Pillar 4: Competition Automation, Cart Gating & Compliance Workflows Question 4.1 (Automated RFQ & Simplified Competition): How do, or could, commercial B2B marketplaces automate competitive quoting for order thresholds exceeding micro-purchase levels ($15,000)? What automated capabilities exist to broadcast quote requests to certified suppliers, enforce competitive response windows, and generate side-by-side price/technical evaluation matrices for buyers? Question 4.2 (Anti-Splitting Surveillance & Purchasing Policy): How can commercial platforms implement algorithmic controls to detect and prevent improper order splitting (e.g., monitoring repeated or related purchases within specific time windows per user, department, or billing code) in accordance with federal purchasing rules (FAR 13.003(c)(2))? Question 4.3 (Approval Workflows & Audit Documentation): How does the system compile and export tamper-evident, permanent requisition records (e.g., PDF/A or structured data packages) to support contract file audits? 4.5 Pillar 5: Interagency Financial Mechanics, Split-Tender & ERP Integration Question 5.1 (Treasury G-Invoicing & Interagency Settlement): How can commercial marketplace platforms interface with federal intergovernmental financial frameworks, specifically U.S. Treasury G-Invoicing (Forms 7600A and 7600B) and IPAC fund settlement? What is industry experience with automated obligation validation prior to cart release? Question 5.2 (Allowance Caps & Multi-Payment Split Checkout): Many civilian agencies provide statutory individual uniform allowances (e.g., under 5 U.S.C. § 5901). How does your platform manage individual employee stipend balances, fiscal-year allowance expirations, and multi-payment split checkouts (e.g., funding an order partially through an agency allowance/GPC and allowing personal card payment for allowable employee out-of-pocket additions under PCI-DSS standards)? Question 5.3 (Cost-Recovery Surcharges & Direct Cash Flow): In a revolving fund model, DLA must recover operating costs through transparent customer surcharges. How do commercial platforms dynamically apply fee markups without inflating base contractor prices, and how can platforms route transaction settlement directly into government accounts without requiring third-party vendor escrow? 4.6 Pillar 6: Cybersecurity, Cloud Accreditation & Acquisition Strategy Question 6.1 (Cloud Hosting & Security Baselines): What is the current cybersecurity authorization level of your solution (e.g., FedRAMP Moderate, FedRAMP High, DoD Cloud SRG Impact Level 4 or 5)? For commercial platforms currently at FedRAMP Moderate or IL-4, what is the feasibility, operational impact, and timeline to achieve or inherit DoD IL-5 compliance for hosting sensitive supply chain and personnel data? Question 6.2 (Enterprise Identity & Back-Office Integration): Describe your platform’s support for Federal PKI, Common Access Card (CAC), and Personal Identity Verification (PIV) single sign-on (SSO). What standard integration methods (e.g., RESTful APIs, ANSI X12 EDI 850/855/856/810, cXML) do you utilize to interface with legacy ERP backbones (such as SAP or Oracle) and SAM.gov vendor verification? Question 6.3 (Commercial Pricing & Agile Acquisition Models): What standard commercial pricing models (e.g., annual SaaS subscription, tiered Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) transaction fees, catalog size licensing, or managed service models) best optimize lifecycle value for the Government? What recommendations does industry have regarding the use of agile acquisition pathways—such as Commercial Solutions Openings (CSOs under 10 U.S.C. § 3458) or Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs under 10 U.S.C. § 4022)—to execute a phased prototype and rapid commercial deployment? Question 6.4 (Operational Capabilities): Will your solution comply with NIST SP 800-53 security controls at the (moderate/high) impact level? Will your solution fully be compliant with Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act (36 CFR 1194)? 4.7 Pillar 7: Past Performance & Notional Models Question 7.1 (Past Performance/Experience): Include a list of relevant past or current contracts, especially with government clients, demonstrating successful execution of building a multiple source ingestion platform. Question 7.2 (Timelines/Pricing Model): Include a notional implementation approach and timeline. What periods of performance would allow reasonable implementation, stabilization, and operations? Include a notional pricing model with cost drivers. 5. Title: FEMA Request for Information - Direct Housing Modernization Capabilities
Description: This Request for Information (RFI) is issued in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulations Overhaul (RFO) 15.101(c). This RFI does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or Request for Quotation (RFQ), and it is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government to enter into a contract, nor will the Government pay for the information submitted in response to this request. All information contained in this RFI is preliminary and is subject to change if, and when, a solicitation is issued. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the U.S. Government to form a binding contract. If a competitive solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) website. It is the responsibility of the interested parties to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to this RFI, or future solicitations. The Department of Homeland Security, Federal Emergency Management Agency, Office of Direct Housing Operations, is conducting market research to identify and seek capabilities from industry in five primary functional areas: Automated Real Estate Aggregation and Vacancy Sourcing - Automated discovery and ingestion of residential rental property listings via Multiple Listing Services (MLS), property management software APIs, commercial rental boards, and direct landlord entry portals. - Real-time vacancy validation to prevent matching against obsolete or unavailable listings. - Rapid geo-fencing within disaster-declared zones and surrounding reasonable-commute perimeters. Artificial Intelligence and Algorithmic Matching - Multi-constraint matching algorithms that pair applicant household profiles with available properties in seconds. - Multi-point geospatial proximity optimization factoring in school district retention, work commutes, medical/provider travel distance, and essential services. - Household composition sizing aligned with HUD Housing Quality Standards (HQS) and FEMA occupancy guidelines. Automated Physical Accessibility Verification - Algorithmic filtering and computer vision inspection tools capable of evaluating floor plans, entry photos, and property specifications against UFAS and ADA physical accessibility standards. - Rapid identification of barrier-free environments, ramps, ground-floor units, grab bars, and wheelchair-accessible kitchens and bathrooms. Landlord Engagement and Leasing Workflow Automation - Automated outreach tools and self-service portals for landlords to submit properties, accept lease terms, and coordinate inspections. - Integration with standard government lease templates and automated electronic signature workflows. Secure Federal Architecture - Enterprise data security architecture compliant with the Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA) at the Moderate impact baseline. - FedRAMP-authorized cloud hosting (or capability to achieve FedRAMP Moderate/High authorization). - Strict data protection for Sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) belonging to disaster survivors.
